To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) music listening-related information in microblogs can be leveraged to estimate artist similarity and popularity, and to cluster artists with regard to additional tag information, (ii) geo-aware interaction can be used to visualize and explore the “world of microblogged music” and (iii) geo-aware interaction is a promising approach to leverage music-related microblogs for music discovery.

we can estimate the popularity of an artist based on the amount of tweets that mention this artist and the popularity of the tags associated with the artist; we can estimate the similarity of two artists by the number of tweets that mention both of them and the number of tweets with tags that are associated with both artists; we can identify trends of music listening based on the number of tweets mentioning an artist; and we can cluster artists with respect of the tags they are associated with and the number of mentions in tweets.

(1) we can use Twitter to estimate artist similarity and popularity, (2) we can cluster artists with respect additional tag information, (3) we can estimate local trends, and (4) we can integrate these diverse pieces of music-related information in a geo-aware user interface to browse music as seen by the Twittersphere.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to make the best out of microblogs with regard to music listening patterns.
the analysis and presentation of music listening patterns in microblog data.
the question of how to exploit music-related microblog data for geospatial analysis and visualization.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the “Twitterspace” is a valuable source of information on music listening patterns, but that the information is highly heterogeneous and noisy and thus, needs to be carefully processed to extract meaningful information.
we have shown that microblog data is an excellent source of information for music listening-related topics.
microblogs are a valuable source of information about music listening patterns, and that the geo-aware music listening patterns can be visualized in a meaningful way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a framework for the analysis of music listening patterns in microblog data.
we are able to extract and integrate music listening information from microblog data, and to visualize it on a geospatial map.
we show that microblog data is a valuable source of information for music listening-related topics and can be leveraged for music listening pattern exploration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
microblog data is a rich source for music listening patterns and trends, which are not necessarily reflected by official music charts.
microblog data can be used as a source to estimate artist similarity as well as popularity.
microblogs can provide rich information for music-related applications, and that geospatial information is an important aspect in this context.
